title: Empirical perm-vs-det uniformity comparison over F_3 / F_5 / F_7
description:
Empirical Monte Carlo comparison of $\operatorname{perm}(A)$ and $\det(A)$ distributions over $\mathbb{F}_q$ for $q \in \{3, 5, 7\}$, reusing the packed permanent kernels built in this epic to validate two distributional claims from the literature. ## Background The reference algorithm paper (arxiv:2407.20205) closes with a Monte Carlo observation that $\operatorname{perm}(A)$ over $\mathbb{F}_3$ tends to the uniform distribution on $\mathbb{F}_3$ as $n \to \infty$ for random $\{-1, 0, 1\}$ matrices. The companion theoretical paper (arxiv:2603.15856, Hunter–Kwan–Sauermann) proves that $\operatorname{perm}(A)$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$ is **significantly more uniform** than $\det(A)$ — quantifying the asymptotic gap. Both claims are testable empirically the moment the epic's packed permanent kernels exist. The harness reuses: - `gf2-algebra::permanent::permanent_bipedal3` for the fast $\mathbb{F}_3$ path. - `gf2-algebra::permanent::permanent_packed5` and `permanent_packed7` for $\mathbb{F}_5$ / $\mathbb{F}_7$. - `gf2_core::field::det` (already exists at `crates/gf2-core/src/field/inverse.rs:526`) for the determinant baseline over `Fp

`. Total-variation distance from uniform is the natural metric: $$ \operatorname{TVD}(\mu, U_{\mathbb{F}_q}) = \frac{1}{2} \sum_{x \in \mathbb{F}_q} \left| \mu(x) - \frac{1}{q} \right| $$ For each $(q, n)$ we estimate $\widehat{\operatorname{TVD}}_{\text{perm}}(n)$ and $\widehat{\operatorname{TVD}}_{\text{det}}(n)$ from $N$ i.i.d. samples and report bootstrap $95\%$ CIs. Sweep grid (target): | $q$ | $n$ values | |-----|----------------------------| | 3 | 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32 | | 5 | 6, 8, 10, 12, 14 | | 7 | 6, 8, 10, 12, 14 | Sample sizes scale to keep the TVD CI half-width $\le 0.01$ for each cell; concrete $N$ values are recorded in the writeup, not pinned in this description. ## Success Criteria - [ ] [hard] `dev/research/perm_uniformity/` exists and builds with `cargo build --manifest-path dev/research/perm_uniformity/Cargo.toml --release` (amended 2026-05-16 from `cargo build -p perm-uniformity --release`; see Amendments §1). - [ ] [hard] The harness consumes the gf2-algebra packed permanents and `gf2_core::field::det` directly — no re-implementation of either. - [ ] [hard] Same RNG seed produces bit-identical **statistical columns** (`q, n, samples, tvd_perm, tvd_perm_ci_lo, tvd_perm_ci_hi, tvd_det, tvd_det_ci_lo, tvd_det_ci_hi`) of the CSV across runs (deterministic reduction across rayon parallelism); the wall-clock timing columns `mean_us_perm` / `mean_us_det` are inherently nondeterministic and excluded from the bit-identical guarantee (amended 2026-05-16; see Amendments §2). - [ ] [hard] Output CSV at `dev/benchmarks/perm_uniformity/results-YYYY-MM-DD.csv` carries columns `q, n, samples, tvd_perm, tvd_perm_ci_lo, tvd_perm_ci_hi, tvd_det, tvd_det_ci_lo, tvd_det_ci_hi, mean_us_perm, mean_us_det` with one row per $(q, n)$ cell of the sweep grid. - [ ] [hard] For $q = 3$ and $n \in \{8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32\}$: $\widehat{\operatorname{TVD}}_{\text{perm}}(n)$ is monotonically non-increasing in $n$ within CI overlap, supporting the $\operatorname{perm} \to U_{\mathbb{F}_3}$ direction. - [ ] [hard] For each $q \in \{3, 5, 7\}$ and each $n \ge 8$ in the sweep: $\widehat{\operatorname{TVD}}_{\text{perm}}(n) \le \widehat{\operatorname{TVD}}_{\text{det}}(n)$ at $95\%$ confidence (one-sided, accounting for the bootstrap CI on the difference), **except the noise-dominated $q=3$ cells $n \in \{24, 28, 32\}$** which are excluded from the verdict (amended 2026-05-16; see Amendments §3). - [ ] [hard] Plot at `dev/benchmarks/perm_uniformity/tvd_vs_n.png` shows both perm and det curves with CI bands, faceted by $q$, log-scale $y$ axis. - [ ] [hard] Writeup at `dev/plans/r3_perm_uniformity_empirical.md` exists, is attached via `jit doc add`, and contains: methodology, chosen sample sizes per cell with justification, observed TVDs with CIs, comparison to the HKS Theorem 1.2 quantitative bound where the asymptotic regime applies, and the deterministic-RNG seed used. - [ ] [hard] `scripts/perm-uniformity-repro.sh` runs end-to-end on the dev host, regenerating the CSV and plot deterministically. - [ ] [hard] User has signed off on the writeup (recorded as a JIT comment) before this issue transitions to `done` — satisfied by the User sign-off note below (2026-05-16). - [ ] [aspirational] Exponential-decay fit for $\mathbb{F}_3$: $\widehat{\operatorname{TVD}}_{\text{perm}}(n) \sim c \cdot \beta^{-n}$ with reported $\beta$ and $c$, plus a discussion of whether the observed $\beta$ matches HKS Theorem 1.2's predicted rate. - [ ] [aspirational] End-to-end repro wall-clock $\le 12$ h on the dev host (AMD Ryzen 9 5900X, 12 physical cores) using the parallel permanent path. ## Notes The two distributional claims are **empirical** in this issue — but per CLAUDE.md, falsification of either by our implementation is more likely to indicate a bug in our packed permanent or our random sampling than a flaw in the theorems. They are therefore tagged `[hard]`, with an $n \ge 8$ guard so very-small-$n$ noise doesn't trip the comparison. If we observe robust falsification at large $n$, the result is itself publishable and the criterion is amended via the standard escalation path. The harness must NOT use a Rust `det` recomputation that diverges from `gf2_core::field::det`; the whole point is to compare against the project's canonical determinant. The harness lives in `dev/research/` rather than as a `gf2-algebra` example because (a) it has heavy dependencies (rayon scheduling, plotting via `plotters` or external matplotlib, statistical bootstrap) inappropriate for the production crate, and (b) sibling research outputs (`dev/research/rns_prototype/`, `dev/research/f5_packing/`) follow this convention. ## Amendments (2026-05-16, user-approved via project-lead escalation) 1. **Criterion 1 (build invocation): `cargo build -p perm-uniformity --release` → `cargo build --manifest-path dev/research/perm_uniformity/Cargo.toml --release`.** Reason: the crate is intentionally excluded from the root workspace (so it does not slow the default `cargo nextest` build); the `-p perm-uniformity` selector fails with "package ID specification did not match any packages". The `--manifest-path` form is the canonical invocation, matching the `permanent_gpu_crossover` / `gf2-kernels-hip` precedents (cf. `.jit/issues/5c0505b2` Amendment 2026-05-15). 2. **Criterion 3 (CSV determinism): bit-identical whole CSV → bit-identical statistical columns.** The guarantee covers `q, n, samples, tvd_perm, tvd_perm_ci_lo, tvd_perm_ci_hi, tvd_det, tvd_det_ci_lo, tvd_det_ci_hi` (seed-pinned, bit-identical across runs including the rayon-parallel reduction). The wall-clock timing columns `mean_us_perm` / `mean_us_det` measure real elapsed time and are inherently nondeterministic; they are explicitly outside the bit-identical guarantee. Reason: timing cannot be bit-reproducible; the scientifically meaningful determinism (TVD estimates + CIs) is fully preserved. 3. **Criterion 6 (TVD_perm ≤ TVD_det for every n ≥ 8): noise-dominated $q=3$ cells $n \in \{24, 28, 32\}$ excluded from the verdict.** The corrected statistic (95th-percentile bootstrap of $\operatorname{TVD}_{\text{perm}} - \operatorname{TVD}_{\text{det}}$; PASS when `diff_q95 < 0`) holds for every cell with adequate $N$. The three $q=3$ large-$n$ cells are sampling-noise-dominated (the $\operatorname{TVD}_{\text{perm}}$ estimator noise floor at $N=500/200/50$ exceeds $\operatorname{TVD}_{\text{det}}/2$), so a 95%-confident comparison is impossible there; per the issue's own escalation clause they are excluded. Observed (from `dev/plans/r3_perm_uniformity_empirical.md` §Criterion 6): $q=3,n=24$ TVD_perm=0.036667 TVD_det=0.086667 diff_q95=−0.005333 (N=500); $n=28$ TVD_perm=0.041667 TVD_det=0.126667 diff_q95=+0.040000 (N=200); $n=32$ TVD_perm=0.133333 TVD_det=0.093333 diff_q95=+0.133333 (N=50). The positive diff_q95 at $n=28/32$ is expected noise at tiny $N$, not a genuine falsification. All other $(q,n)$ cells PASS with comfortable margin (diff_q95 ≤ −0.005333; most ≤ −0.03). ## User sign-off (criterion 10) **2026-05-16:** The user signed off on the writeup `dev/plans/r3_perm_uniformity_empirical.md` and approved Amendments §1–§3 above, via the project-lead escalation path (AskUserQuestion answers: "You amend criterion 1" / "Stats-only determinism OK" / "Accept noise-exclusion" / "Sign off"). This satisfies the criterion-10 sign-off requirement (recorded here as the JIT approval record).
